summary: Herbert Niel Randle was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1910–1927) and as Librarian at the India Office Records (1927–1949) and the India Office (~1933–1949).

Herbert V. Guenther specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Munich and Vienna under Geiger, Wüst, and Havers, he held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Saskatchewan, where he headed Far Eastern Studies (1964–1984).

Herbert Weir Smyth was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe. His career included posts at Williams College, Bryn Mawr, and Harvard, where he became Eliot Professor of Greek Literature.
Herbert Zachert was a Japanologist who studied under Karl Florenz (~1928–1933). He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1949–1960) and the University of Bonn (~1960–1977).

Herman Kellgren was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe Édouard Foucaux, and held a post at the University of Helsinki from circa 1849 to 1856.

Hermann Beckh worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kiel and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD ~1902–1907), he held posts at the Kiel Institute, the Royal Library of Berlin, and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1916–1921).

Hermann Berger was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Helmut Hoffmann (~1950–1953) for his doctorate and habilitation. He later held a post at Heidelberg University from approximately 1964 to 1992.
Hermann Beythan was an Indologist and linguist who studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai.

Hermann Bonitz was a philosopher who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1831–1834) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1834–1836). He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (~1867–1888).

Hermann Brockhaus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He held professorships at the University of Jena (1839) and the University of Leipzig (1848, 1872–1877), and co-founded the DMG.

Hermann Brunnhofer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Zurich, as well as under Albrecht Weber. His career included positions at Saint Petersburg State University and as a lecturer at the University of Bern (1901–1914).
Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1860–1864). He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau from approximately 1866 to 1904.

Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Halle under Benfey, Fick, Sauppe, and Bezzenberger. Collitz held posts at Bryn Mawr College and Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928), and co-founded the Linguistic Society of America.
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1877–1882) and later held a post as professor at the University of Giessen (~1904–1922).

Hermann Goetz was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Munich and under Jean Philippe Vogel. He served as curator at the Baroda Museum, director of the National Gallery of Modern Art, and director of art history at Heidelberg University.

Hermann Grassmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher and spent much of his teaching career at the Marienstiftsgymnasium, serving as professor from 1852 to 1877.
Hermann Güntert was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1921–1923) and Heidelberg University (~1923–1948).

Hermann Hirt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Freiburg and Leipzig. He served as Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig (1891–1912) and as professor of Sanskrit and Indo-European linguistics at the University of Giessen (1912–1936).

Hermann Hunger is an archaeologist and linguist who studied at Vienna, Heidelberg, and Münster. He held positions at the German Archaeological Institute, the University of Chicago (~1970–1978), and the University of Vienna (~1978–2007).

Hermann Hupfeld was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Marburg and Halle-Wittenberg, and subsequently held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1825–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1843–1866).
